plotSections.title: Gerk Experiments with the Keystone
bullets: Gerk begins experimenting with his new ability to open portals through doors. His first attempt opens onto a murky, brackish body of water, producing a powerful rush of swamp water that blasts Sylan across the room before Gerk closes the portal.

A second, more cautious portal opens onto a barren, rocky landscape filled with geysers. Steam, intense heat, and a sulfuric/brimstone smell spill through the opening, demonstrating that Gerk can potentially access radically different environments.

The portals are formed by Gerk interacting with a tangible-looking door that is actually a reflection of the world being opened into; the door materializes as he turns the handle rather than being a normal physical doorway.

The DM establishes that opening or closing a portal is an action for combat purposes. Gerk and Sylan recognize the potential tactical uses and dangers of the ability and plan to practice during the voyage.
Gerk intends to experiment with opening portals to familiar locations by concentrating on them, beginning with the party's house.

plotSections.title: The Party Leaves the Gatehouse
bullets: Walker, Glimmen, Plymouth Gawater, Elrus, and Araden leave to investigate the training grounds associated with the guild of dragon riders and the origins of Grixto and Galixtar.
Sylan speaks with Juten Prime before departing and confirms that the party will take guardianship of the keystones they have claimed while leaving the remaining two keystones in Juten Prime's care.

Juten Prime agrees to safeguard the two keystones left behind and continue investigating the site, though Plymouth will likely need to return to verify their findings. The party agrees to exchange updates when possible.

Dana determines that there is little remaining in the ruined archives worth studying immediately, but wants to speak with Plymouth later about what he has learned regarding the gatehouse and its history.

plotSections.title: Ruined Archives and the Keystone Investigation
bullets: The former libraries and archives of the mountain are largely destroyed. Evidence indicates both deliberate raiding and natural degradation over time, with paper and similar materials mostly deteriorated and stone, slate, and tile records either broken or removed.
Only roughly the upper third of the mountain has been explored so far, leaving substantial portions of the site unexplored.
Sylan theorizes that Grixto may have learned how to use the keystones through information contained in the site's archives, potentially explaining his knowledge of them.

plotSections.title: Return to Langdale Stronghold
bullets: The party boards the boat for an approximately five-day journey to Langdale Stronghold.

Because time in Midgar moves at a different rate, one day in Midgar corresponds to seven days there. Walker, having left expecting to have a full week, intends to take advantage of the difference and potentially remain away for much longer from the party's perspective.
During the voyage, Gerk plans to practice his portal ability while Sylan helps him experiment with safer and more controlled techniques.

chronologicalEvents: Walker has Glimmen carry Plymouth Gawater through a portal while Walker follows, after which Plymouth, Walker, Glimmen, Elrus, and Araden leave to investigate the dragon-rider training grounds and the origins of Grixto and Galixtar.
Sylan decides the party should speak with Juten Prime before leaving and asks whether Juten Prime can safeguard the two keystones the party is leaving behind.
Juten Prime agrees to protect the two remaining keystones and continue investigating the site, with Plymouth expected to verify the work later.
Gerk experiments with his portal ability and accidentally opens a portal to brackish swamp water, blasting Sylan with water before closing it.
Gerk opens another portal more carefully, revealing a hot, barren landscape with geysers, steam, sulfur, and brimstone.
The DM clarifies that opening and closing the portal is an action in combat.
Sylan and Gerk discuss possible combat applications and dangers of the portals, including using environmental hazards against enemies.
Dana asks whether the site has an intact library; she learns that the former libraries and archives are largely destroyed.
The party learns that the archives were damaged through a combination of raiding and natural degradation, and that only about the upper third of the mountain has been explored.
Sylan theorizes that Grixto may have learned to use the keystones through the site's archives.
The party begins the five-day journey by boat back to Langdale Stronghold.
The party discusses Midgar's time differential, where one day corresponds to seven days elsewhere, and Walker plans to exploit the extra apparent time for his own activities.
Gerk and Sylan plan to use the journey to practice and refine Gerk's portal ability.
Gerk decides to attempt opening a portal to the party's house by concentrating on the familiar location.

He is beginning to experiment with controlling where and how the portals open and intends to practice during the voyage.
He plans to test whether concentrating on a familiar location, such as the party's house, can cause a portal to open there.

Willing to experiment repeatedly, even after an initially dangerous result.

newTerms.name: Gerk's Portal Doors
notes: Gerk can manifest a door-like reflection of reality that opens into another location or environment.
Opening and closing a portal requires an action in combat.
The destination can produce physical environmental effects, such as flooding, steam, heat, or other hazards.

newTerms.name: Midgar Time Differential
notes: One day in Midgar corresponds to seven days outside Midgar, significantly affecting travel and the amount of time characters can experience while away.
